```{python}
#| label: fig-tank-bandpass
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Input impedance of an N-path filter, obtained by frequency-translating the first-order baseband $RC$ impedance to $\\pm f_\\mathrm{LO}$ and adding the series switch resistance. Doubling the path capacitance halves the bandwidth, while the peak impedance stays at $R_\\mathrm{sw} + R_\\mathrm{BB}$."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ---------- model ----------
# A passive mixer is "transparent": the impedance connected at baseband appears
# at the RF port, shifted up to +/- f_LO. With a first-order baseband load
#   Z_BB(df) = R_BB / (1 + j*2*pi*df*R_BB*C)
# the RF-port impedance around the LO becomes
#   Z_in(f_LO + df) = R_sw + Z_BB(df)
# i.e. a *first-order* bandpass centred exactly at f_LO.
#
# Everything is normalised to R_sw = 1 and f_LO = 1.
R_sw = 1.0     # on-resistance of one switch
R_BB = 20.0    # effective shunt resistance at baseband (sets the peak impedance)
f_LO = 1.0

# Baseband pole placed at 1 % of f_LO for the reference capacitance C0
f_pole_C0 = 0.01 * f_LO           # = 1 / (2*pi*R_BB*C0)

f = np.linspace(0.90, 1.10, 4000)

def Z_in(f, f_pole):
    """Magnitude of the N-path input impedance, normalised to R_sw."""
    df = f - f_LO
    Z_bb = R_BB / (1.0 + 1j * df / f_pole)
    return np.abs(R_sw + Z_bb) / R_sw

Z_C0 = Z_in(f, f_pole_C0)          # capacitance C0
Z_2C0 = Z_in(f, f_pole_C0 / 2.0)   # capacitance 2*C0 -> pole at half the frequency

Z_peak = (R_sw + R_BB) / R_sw      # peak impedance, normalised to R_sw
Z_3dB = Z_peak / np.sqrt(2.0)

# ---------- plot ----------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=(6, 4))

ax.plot(f, Z_C0, 'b-', linewidth=2.5, label=r'$C$')
ax.plot(f, Z_2C0, 'g-', linewidth=2.0, alpha=0.8, label=r'$2C$ (half the bandwidth)')

ax.axhline(Z_3dB, color='gray', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6, linewidth=1)
ax.text(0.905, Z_3dB + 0.5, '-3 dB', color='gray')
ax.axvline(f_LO, color='gray', linestyle=':', alpha=0.6, linewidth=1)

ax.plot(f_LO, Z_peak, 'ro', markersize=7)
ax.annotate(r'peak $= (R_\mathrm{sw} + R_\mathrm{BB}) / R_\mathrm{sw}$',
            xy=(f_LO, Z_peak), xytext=(0.905, Z_peak - 1.2),
            color='red', ha='left', va='center',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='red', lw=1.2))

# Mark the -3 dB bandwidth of the C curve
half_bw = f_pole_C0
ax.annotate('', xy=(f_LO + half_bw, Z_3dB), xytext=(f_LO - half_bw, Z_3dB),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='<->', color='blue', lw=1.8))
ax.text(f_LO, Z_3dB - 2.0, r'BW $= 1/(\pi R_\mathrm{BB} C) \propto 1/C$',
        ha='center', va='top', color='blue',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='lightblue', alpha=0.7))

ax.set_xlabel(r'Frequency (normalized to $f_\mathrm{LO}$)')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$| Z_\mathrm{in} | / R_\mathrm{sw}$')
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax.legend(loc='lower right')
ax.set_xlim(0.90, 1.10)
ax.set_ylim(0, Z_peak * 1.15)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
